case_facts.operation: Wilsey Ranch is a labor-constrained cow-calf and American Wagyu/Akagushi-influenced direct-market operation near Marsing, Idaho.
case_facts.people: Lisa Wilsey and her mother Debby carry the regular workload; family help appears mainly around high-intensity events such as branding and weaning.
case_facts.business_model: Direct-to-consumer and cooperative-market orientation with premium meat, tallow products, and local-market/customer-trust demands.
case_facts.terrain_and_infrastructure: Rough or uneven ground, pasture-to-pasture moves, trees/brush/signal concerns, and prior experience with temporary electric fencing that did not fit all cattle behavior.
case_facts.identity_tension: Virtual fencing may preserve the ranch by easing labor and improving grazing control, but it also changes what ranching feels like and what skills are central.

nofence.rough_case_estimate: 60-collar starter package about $20,748 in year 1 and about $1,920 per year thereafter.

vence.rough_case_estimate: 250 head about $10,000 per year subscription plus base station/setup.
vence.likely_use: Whole-herd or larger pilot where infrastructure fits.

halter.rough_case_estimate: 250 head about $15,000 per year subscription plus towers.
halter.likely_use: Higher-service virtual fencing and monitoring model, dependent on tower/cell fit.

typical_cost_points: Collars often range around $200-329 per head depending on vendor/species.
Base stations or towers can run $5,000-10,000 each.
Physical fence can exceed $30,000 per mile in some contexts.
labor_outcome_examples: Summer gather reported from 7 days at 85% success to 3.5 days at 100% success.
2,000-acre gather reported from 3-5 days with 3-5 people to 4 hours with 2 people, a 90-95% labor-day reduction.
Range gather reported from 2-3 weeks to 5 days, a 67-75% reduction.
One large early-adopter comparison reported gathering time dropping from 3 months to 2.5 weeks.
One case eliminated weekly perimeter checks across 26 gates.
reliability_and_failure_examples: One Vence year-2 case had roughly 40% collar failure in a season.
A repaired/current Vence example reported roughly 98% working collars.
A Halter example reported 1-3 failures out of 300 collars, about 0.3-1%.
Signal dead zones can remove large terrain sections from practical use.
GPS/cell variability can create animal-welfare problems if animals are punished near water or in poor-signal areas.
ecological_outcomes_examples: Medusa head cover reduction from about 25% to under 10%.
Forage production increase from about 3,000 lbs/acre to 8,000 lbs/acre.
Barbed goat grass seed heads reduced from about 16 per plant to 1-2.
Fuel load reduction from about 4,300 lbs/acre to 800 lbs/acre.

wilsey_specific_economic_texture.wagyu_finish_time: Wagyu-influenced cattle may take about 30 months to finish compared with roughly 18 months or less in conventional systems.
why_it_matters: More months of feed, pasture, monitoring, and health risk.
More capital tied up per animal.
Higher value of avoided loss and better grazing distribution.
Longer exposure to market, drought, and labor shocks.
wilsey_specific_economic_texture.bull_adaptation: Imported Akagushi/Wagyu bulls may look valuable genetically but can take time to acclimate and may be harder to handle; locally adapted bulls can be cheaper, safer, easier, and better trained.
wilsey_specific_economic_texture.dna_testing: DNA testing around $50 per cow was discontinued when market requirements no longer justified it.
wilsey_specific_economic_texture.hay_decision: Buying hay versus growing hay is a combined cost, labor, equipment, fire-risk, and herd-size decision, not only a feed-price decision.

pilot_design.decision_rule_needed: A pilot must define what result means stop, continue, or scale.
test_hard_conditions: Pastures where water, brush, or draws complicate GPS/cell performance.
Bottleneck labor weeks, not only easy months.
metrics: Escapes or boundary failures by severity.
Human hours before and after, including troubleshooting.
Whether Lisa and Debby actually get time back in the hardest weeks.
